events.kind: state audit office audit of the bank
events.summary: The State Audit Office (Drzaven zavod za revizija) audited the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia's 2003 financial statements, auditing on site from 12 October to 20 December 2004 under article 2 of the Law on State Audit. Its final report, number 11-107/8 of 4 March 2005, has a section headed improper and unlawful use of funds: it found the National Bank had guaranteed a domestic bank with foreign-currency deposits, and that in January 2004 the foreign banks drew 20,759,515 US dollars from the National Bank's guarantee deposit. It also found that 30,210 thousand denars of purchases, 35.61 percent of the purchases audited, were made without following the Public Procurement Law, and told the bank to give up commercial activities that article 83 of the Law on the National Bank does not allow it.

events.kind: law change the bank objected to in writing
events.summary: Samoa's government pressed ahead with changes to the central bank's law that would widen the Finance Minister's role and move some of the bank's rules into regulations. In a letter to the Attorney-General's office the Central Bank of Samoa said the changes had come as a surprise and warned they could weaken its independence, increase political influence and create legal uncertainty. The IMF wrote to Finance Minister Mulipola Anarosa Ale Molio'o on 9 April 2026 warning the reforms could weaken the bank's autonomy; Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt rejected the warnings as outside interference.

events.summary: During the question-and-answer session after her State of the Nation Address, President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah said the reported losses at the Bank of Namibia, together with missing Government Institutions Pension Fund money, were smelling of corruption and must be investigated. Affirmative Repositioning leader Job Amupanda said the central bank had made a loss close to a billion dollars for unexplained reasons. The report does not say who would carry out any investigation or that one was formally ordered.

searched_none.note: Read the AFP currency-controls dispatch on Sudan Tribune (no issuing authority named, no year: 'all transactions in Eritrea shall be settled in nakfa', the Bank of Eritrea named only as the body that may grant exemptions) and VOA of 25 November 2015 on the 2015 banknote exchange, which credits the decision to the Bank of Eritrea itself ('The Bank of Eritrea recently announced that all Nakfa notes in circulation must be exchanged') and attributes the withdrawal limits only to 'the new law' without naming who passed it. The IMF's 2009 Article IV notice (PIN 09/133) says 'Directors regretted that monetary policy remains dominated by government financing needs' and 'Restoring the independence of monetary policy was viewed as critical', and the 2019 Article IV call to 'reinstate the central bank's independence' is behind a Central Banking paywall; both are characterisations that never name the Bank of Eritrea or any dated act. The Library of Congress holds Eritrean proclamations individually but 91/1996 is the Eritrean Development and Investment Bank, and no proclamation establishing the Bank of Eritrea is online. ONE FACT WOULD REVERSE THIS: the text of the Bank of Eritrea proclamation showing who appoints and removes the governor or whether the government may instruct the bank (try the Library of Congress Eritrean proclamation series by number, e.g. the 1993-1997 range around notice 15/1993, and the Gazette of Eritrean Laws), or a dated removal or replacement of a named governor of the Bank of Eritrea.

Held again, not refiled on the statute as instructed. Searched in Portuguese and English for an episode: a governor pressed out, an investigation of the bank, functions or money taken, a public demand, or a law the bank objected to. Central Banking of 8 September 2023, relaying Lusa, reports Helder Lopes expected to succeed Abrao de Vasconcelos but 'does not say why' and names no removing body, so it is an appointment and excluded. Lusa/Tatoli of 8 May 2026 on the Petroleum Fund describes only the ordinary division of labour: 'the Ministry of Finance sets the investment strategy' while 'the Central Bank of Timor-Leste carries out the operational management of investments', and 'The national parliament must approve all transfers from the Petroleum Fund'. ONE FACT WOULD REVERSE THIS: the article of the Petroleum Fund Law (Law 9/2005 as amended) that puts the investment strategy in the Minister of Finance's hands with the BCTL only executing it, which would be a standing statutory arrangement over part of the bank's work and sits outside the no-instructions clause of the BCTL's own law; the text is at mj.gov.tl/jornal (SERIE I) and laohamutuk.org. Failing that, a Parlamento Nacional committee minute summoning the governor or ordering an inquiry into the bank.

A record is filed for the President's public statement of 13 April 2026. The standing power in section 66(2) and (3) of the Bank of Namibia Act 1 of 2020 is still only a power: searched the Auditor-General's output, parliament.na and the Namibian press and found no instance of a Minister directing the Auditor-General to investigate the bank's accounts or affairs. ONE FACT WOULD REVERSE THAT SEPARATE RECORD: an Auditor-General report or a National Assembly minute recording a Minister of Finance request or direction under section 66 of the 2020 Act. Also checked and excluded: the N$1 million fine on Governor Johannes Gawaxab and the board's clearing of him, which is a regulator acting on a governor's own private business, excluded by rule 10.

A record is filed from the State Audit Office's own final report on the National Bank. The 2025 Law on the National Bank in Gazette 16/25 was not obtained: nbrm.mk refuses both the PDF and the .docx of its own law with a client error, and no gazette host returned the article text, so no direction power, profit share or at-will dismissal clause could be confirmed. ONE FACT WOULD REVERSE A SECOND RECORD: the text of the article of Sluzben vesnik 16/25 that gives the Government or the Assembly a direction power over the National Bank, a share of its profit, or dismissal of the governor at will. The State Audit Office site dzr.mk and its archive arhiva.dzr.mk are open to automation and hold further reports.

A record is filed for the April 2026 rewrite that the Central Bank of Samoa objected to in writing. Not filed as a second record, to avoid doubling the same episode: PMN of 19 August 2026 reports the second reading of the Central Bank of Samoa Amendment Bill 2026, at which Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt said 'The CBS belongs to the government of Samoa'. The bill as described does not qualify on its own terms: removal grounds are listed, policy disagreement cannot be a ground, an independent panel must investigate first, and the quarterly reports to the Minister 'do not give the Minister power to direct the Bank'. ONE FACT WOULD MAKE IT A SEPARATE RECORD: the enacted text of the Central Bank of Samoa Amendment Act 2026 as passed, if it differs from the bill by giving the Minister or Cabinet a direction power or removal at will.
